title: Tiling basics for handymen: tile check, cut and fix
audience: Handyman workers doing basic tiling and tiling trades workers at the basic level
learningOutcomes: Check tiles and the substrate for size, flatness and condition before fixing.
Cut and fix tiles on a dry, sound substrate with the correct adhesive and spacing.
Identify when a wet area or waterproofing task is referred under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”.

instruction.heading: Check the tile and the substrate first
instruction.body: Before fixing, check the tiles for size, thickness, flatness, colour and any chips or cracks. Lay out a dry run and check the set-out so that cut tiles are not too narrow at the edges. Check the substrate: it must be flat, sound, clean, dry and firm. Tiling over a loose, damp, dusty or deflecting surface gives tiles that lift or crack. Note any substrate fault and fix or refer it before tiling begins.

instruction.heading: Cut and fix
instruction.body: Cut tiles with a suitable cutter or wet saw, and check each cut against the layout. Spread adhesive with a notched trowel suited to the tile size, and back-butter large tiles where the data sheet requires it. Press each tile into the adhesive and use spacers to keep joints even. Check the tiles are level with a straight edge as you go, and correct lipping while the adhesive is workable. Allow the adhesive to set for the time the data sheet gives before grouting or walking on the surface.

instruction.heading: Where tiling stops and referral starts
instruction.body: Wet areas and waterproofing are not covered by this basic lesson. Where tiles are to be fixed in a shower, around a bath, or in an area that needs a waterproof membrane, refer under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”, because the waterproofing position is recorded as needing a licence check. Before you accept any tiling work, check the licence position for its value in your state. In New South Wales the contractor licence applies above $5,000 of labour and materials, GST included, as the NSW Government page last updated on 23 June 2026 shows. Do not tile over a waterproofing system that you cannot identify.

procedure: Check the tiles for size, flatness and damage, and reject any that are defective.
Check the substrate is flat, sound, clean and dry.
Lay out a dry run and set out the first row to avoid narrow edge cuts.
Cut tiles to the layout with the correct tool, and check each cut.
Spread adhesive with the correct trowel, press tiles in with spacers, and check level as you go.
Refer any wet-area or waterproofing task under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”, and record the referral.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks you to tile a bathroom floor and the shower recess, and says the membrane was done by a previous worker.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the tiling go ahead as a basic tiling job?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not as a basic job. The shower recess is a wet area that depends on the waterproofing position, and the membrane's condition is unknown. Refer the wet area under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”, confirm the waterproofing position, and record it. The dry floor can be assessed separately.

equipmentAndPpe: Notched trowel, spacers and straight edge
Tile cutter or wet saw with water supply

commonErrors.error: Tiling over a loose, damp or dusty substrate.
commonErrors.prevention: Check and prepare the substrate, and refer any defect.

commonErrors.error: Setting out without a dry run, leaving narrow edge cuts.
commonErrors.prevention: Lay out a dry run and adjust the set-out before fixing.

commonErrors.error: Tiling a wet area without confirming the waterproofing position.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer wet areas under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence positions for wall and floor tiling. New South Wales: a contractor licence is needed for tiling work where labour and materials, GST included, exceed $5,000 (NSW Government page, last updated 23 June 2026). Queensland: wall and floor tiling is a QBCC licence class (class page last reviewed 31 August 2021). The $3,300 figure on that page limits incidental work outside the class; it is not a tiling threshold. Victoria: a tiling-only job needs no registration, but combining tiling with another trade on one job does (Consumer Victoria page, last updated 9 July 2025). South Australia: anyone carrying on business as a building work contractor needs a licence; the CBS guide gives no dollar threshold and does not name tiling (no date shown).
Silica dust from cutting tile is controlled as set out in “Cutting tile and silica dust controls”.
Completing this lesson does not give a tiling licence, certificate or authority to waterproof or tile wet areas.

qualityStandard: The tiles are checked and defective tiles rejected before fixing.
The substrate is flat, sound, clean and dry before tiling.
Wet areas are referred and not tiled as basic work.
documentationEvidence: Tile set-out and product record with adhesive and spacing
Referral note for any wet area
summary: Check the tiles and the substrate before fixing.
Cut, fix and check level with the correct adhesive and spacing.
Refer wet areas and waterproofing under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for a shower recess to be tiled and says the membrane was done previously. What is correct?
options: Refer the wet area under the waterproofing check before tiling it
Tile it as a basic job with no checks needed at all on the day of the job
Tile it without checking the membrane underneath the tiles at all
Paint the recess instead of tiling it at all in the bathroom

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a dry run carried out before fixing?
options: To check the adhesive colour before the fix
To set out the first row and avoid narrow edge cuts
To see whether the client likes the tile colour
It is not necessary at all on any tiling job

knowledgeChecks.question: What must the substrate be before tiles are fixed, according to the lesson?
options: Loose, so the tiles can settle
Flat, sound, clean, dry and firm
Any surface, if the adhesive is strong enough
